svg.title: Accepted-loan preprocessing architecture
svg.text: Accepted-loan preprocessing: architecture
AI Credit Risk / Loan Approval Engine · read top to bottom · blue = original notebook (Steps 1-10, kept) · orange = review · green = Preprocessing V2 · purple = audits
Load the raw data and define the prediction point
notebooks/accepted_preprocessing.ipynb · Step 1
Loaded LendingClub accepted_2007_to_2018Q4.csv: 2,260,701 loans × 151 columns.
Ground rule for the whole project: the model scores a NEW application, so it may only use information that exists at or before the application / underwriting
decision. Every later step enforces this rule.
Investigate loan_status (what happened to each loan)
Step 2
9 distinct statuses + 33 missing values:
Fully Paid
Current (still running)
Charged Off
Late (31-120 / 16-30 days) + In Grace Period
'Does not meet the credit policy' (Fully Paid / Charged Off)
Default
Define the target (what the model predicts)
Step 3
target = 0 (good): Fully Paid, 'Does not meet the credit policy. Status: Fully Paid'.
target = 1 (bad / default): Charged Off, Default, 'Does not meet the credit policy. Status: Charged Off'.
No target: Current, Late, In Grace Period, missing. These loans have no final outcome yet, so labelling them would be guessing.
Define the eligible population (only loans with a final outcome)
Step 4
Kept 1,348,099 resolved loans (59.63% of all rows) and dropped 912,602 unresolved ones.
Class balance: 1,078,739 good (80.0%) vs 269,360 default (20.0%).
Audit every column
Step 5
For all 152 columns (151 + target): data type, missing count and %, number of unique values, sample values.
Found 40 columns ≥ 80% missing and 7 constant / single-value columns.
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_column_audit.csv
Application-time vs future-time audit (the leakage review)
Step 6
Every column was put in exactly one class, by asking: would we know this value when the application arrives?
94 application-time features: income, DTI, FICO, credit-bureau history, loan amount, purpose, state, ...
42 post-prediction columns, only known AFTER the loan starts: payments received, recoveries, outstanding principal, last payment / last FICO / last credit
pull, hardship plans, debt settlement, funded amounts, issue_d.
4 LendingClub-derived columns kept for review: int_rate, installment, grade, sub_grade (LendingClub's own risk view).
Other: 4 text / high-cardinality (emp_title, desc, title, zip_code), 1 historical date (earliest_cr_line), 2 target (loan_status, target), 2 identifiers (id,
member_id), 3 administrative (url, policy_code, initial_list_status).
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_timing_audit.csv
Remove target, leakage, identifiers and administrative columns
Step 7
Dropped 49 columns = 2 target + 2 identifiers + 3 administrative + 42 post-prediction. Result: 1,348,099 rows × 103 candidate columns. Checks confirmed no target,
id or future column remains.
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_step7_removal_audit.csv, data/interim/accepted_model_candidates.csv
Data-quality investigation
Step 8
Checked missingness, all-missing columns, constant columns, duplicate column names, columns with identical content, duplicate rows, infinite values, numeric
ranges and categorical cardinality. Nothing needed removing, so the dataset stays 1,348,099 × 103.
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_step8_quality_audit.csv, data/interim/accepted_quality_clean.csv (V2 input)
Feature semantics and representation plan
Step 9
Each column labelled numeric / categorical / date / free text / LendingClub-derived, with a planned treatment. Key decisions: desc (free text) is left out of the
first version because it needs NLP; earliest_cr_line becomes a date-based feature; emp_title / title need a high-cardinality encoder.
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_step9_representation_plan.csv
Missing-value strategy
Step 10
Columns bucketed by missingness, with a strategy for each. Rule carried into V2: every imputation value (median, category, ...) must be learned from TRAINING data
only, never from validation or test.
Output: reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_step10_missing_audit.csv, reports/preprocessing_v1_audits/accepted_step10_missing_strategy.csv
Why V1 Steps 11-16 were replaced by Preprocessing V2
review outcome
V1 finished with a random 80/10/10 split and 1,943 columns, but a review found five problems:
the labels (y) were never exported, so a modeling notebook could not load them;
earliest_cr_line (a date like 'Aug-2003') was one-hot encoded into 733 columns instead of one number;
zip_code was one-hot encoded into 936 columns;
the final fitted encoders and medians were never saved, so a new application could not be scored;
the random split mixes years; credit-risk models should be tested on LATER loans than they were trained on.
V1 outputs are kept untouched as a backup: final_preprocessed_data/, processed_data/, step13_artifacts/.
Data restoration: re-attach id, issue_d and target safely
src/preprocessing_v2/restore.py
accepted_quality_clean.csv has no id, issue_d or target (Step 7 removed them). The raw CSV is re-read in its original order and filtered with the same target
mapping: 1,348,099 eligible rows.
Safety check before attaching anything by position: 12 shared columns (loan_amnt, int_rate, annual_inc, dti, revol_util, fico_range_low, term, grade, emp_title,
title, zip_code, earliest_cr_line) are compared row by row. Result: 0 mismatches, ids unique, every issue_d parses. Any mismatch would stop the run.
Temporal split by loan issue month
split.py
Train on older loans, validate and test on newer ones, the way the model will actually be used:
Split
Issue months
Rows
Defaults
Default rate
Train
Validation
Test
Stress test only
Excluded
Why train starts in Aug-2012: 33 credit-bureau fields (tot_cur_bal, num_*, mo_sin_*, ...) only start being filled in Mar-Aug 2012. Earlier loans would teach
the model that 'missing' means 'old loan'.
Why 2016-2018 is not the test set: at the 2018Q4 snapshot only 67.5% of 2016 loans (38% of 2017, 11% of 2018) had finished. The finished ones are mostly early
defaults and early payoffs, so their default rate is distorted.
Every split has plenty of defaults (≥ 33k), so no resampling is needed.
Feature engineering (row by row, nothing learned from data)
features.py
credit_history_months = (issue_year − ecl_year) × 12 + (issue_month − ecl_month), using the application month. Replaces the 733 date columns with ONE number.
Train: no missing, no negatives, range 36-842, median 177.
term_months: ' 36 months' → 36, ' 60 months' → 60. emp_length_years: '< 1 year' → 0 ... '10+ years' → 10.
Text categories stripped; zip_code / emp_title / title lowercased so 'Teacher' and 'teacher ' are the same value.
All other columns converted to numbers; raw dates, id, issue_d and desc dropped.
This exact function lives INSIDE the saved pipeline, so a new application goes through the same steps.
Fitted preprocessing: one scikit-learn Pipeline, fitted on TRAIN only
pipeline.py
fit_transform(X_train, y_train) is the only fit. Validation, test and stress rows are only ever transformed.
a) Train-only column filter: drop columns > 95% missing or constant in TRAIN (31 dropped)
application_type (only 'Individual' in train); 4 joint-application + 11 second-applicant columns + sec_app_credit_history_months (joint applications started
later);
14 newer credit-bureau columns (open_acc_6m, il_util, all_util, inq_fi, ...) that LendingClub only began reporting in late 2015.
b) ColumnTransformer: three branches
Numeric (62 columns): fill missing values with the TRAIN median, plus a 0/1 'was missing' flag (missing often means 'never happened', e.g. months since last
delinquency).
One-hot (6 columns): grade 7, sub_grade 33, home_ownership 4, verification_status 3, purpose 13, addr_state 47. Categories with < 500 training rows are
grouped as 'infrequent'; unseen ones map safely.
Target encoding (zip_code, emp_title, title): each category becomes its smoothed TRAIN default rate. Training rows use 5-fold out-of-fold values (a row never
sees its own label); val/test use the train-only mapping; unseen categories get the overall train default rate (17.24%).
c) Drop duplicate columns: 17 'was missing' flags were identical to another flag in TRAIN
Result: 103 raw input columns → 190 numeric model features.
Artifact saving
export.py
preprocessor_v2.joblib: the whole fitted pipeline in one file (feature engineering + filter + encoders + dedupe).
metadata_v2.json: split windows and statistics, input columns, the 190 feature names, feature groups (incl. the 42 LendingClub risk columns for the
with/without comparison), parameters, library versions.
Output: artifacts_v2/preprocessor_v2.joblib, metadata_v2.json, feature_list_v2.csv
Export every split
export.py
Each split is transformed (validation / test / stress in 100k-row chunks to save memory), written, then read back and checked.
X_<split>.parquet: the 190 features only.
y_<split>.parquet: id, issue_d, target, in exactly the same row order as X.
Output: final_preprocessed_data_v2/ (train, validation, test, stress_2016_2018)
Final audits: 72 checks, 0 failed, 0 warnings
audits.py
Target alignment (20): raw vs Step 10 rows identical; X rows = y rows; target only 0/1; 1,000 random ids match the raw loan_status and issue_d 100%.
Temporal ordering (8): every row inside its window; 2014-12 < 2015-01, 2015-06 < 2015-07, 2015-12 < 2016-01; no id in two splits.
Leakage (9): no target / id / date / post-loan column among features; medians, categories, filter decisions and the encoder prior all reproduce from TRAIN
alone; training-row target encodings are out-of-fold. Highest single-feature AUC = 0.674 (int_rate), under the 0.80 review flag.
Data hygiene (17): 0 NaN, 0 infinite, 0 non-numeric, 0 duplicate columns in every split.
Consistency (9): 190 features in identical order in every file and in the metadata.
Persistence and backups (4): reloaded pipeline gives identical output; V1 backup files unchanged.
Engineering, readiness, fresh session (5): no negative credit history; term ∈ {36, 60}; every emp_length mapped; LendingClub risk columns available; fresh-
process test passed.
Output: artifacts_v2/audit_report_v2.json, preprocessing_v2_report.md, single_feature_auc_v2.csv
Fresh-session inference test (separate Python process)
tests/fresh_session_inference_test.py
Loads preprocessor_v2.joblib with no notebook state.
Raw CSV rows for 5 test loans reproduce the exported X_test rows exactly (max difference 0.0).
A hand-written NEW application gives 1 row × 190 features with no NaN: unseen zip '000xx' → train default rate 0.1724; missing emp_title → its learned
'missing' value; missing dti → train median 17.26; Mar-2010 → Oct-2026 = 199 months of credit history.
Next: model preparation (not started)
Model A uses all 190 features; model B drops the 42 LendingClub risk columns (grade, sub_grade, int_rate, installment) to show what the model learns on its
own.
Logistic Regression baseline (needs a scaler) → LightGBM / XGBoost; class weights for the 17-20% default rate.
Tune on validation, test once on test, calibrate probabilities, report results for 36- vs 60-month loans separately, optionally check on the 2016-2018 stress
set.
